Strait of Hormuz Status: October 5, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief
Skip to content Straits Hormuz Live Monitor Day  218 Open? Live map News About Method API Live

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
5 October 2026 .
Brent $ 101.84 -0.40 % · Transits 1 (2026-09-27) · AI-assisted
01 All U.S. bombers have left a UK air base amid suspected terror plot concerns and more tankers were struck near Iran, per CNBC, not independently confirmed in this feed.

02 Iran's conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz include halting U.S. aggression, ending the naval blockade, and releasing Iranian assets, per CNBC; Fox News, India Today, and TheCable carry related reporting.

03 The physical transit picture remains contested: Ghalibaf says the strait stays closed until Iran's seven conditions are met, while thenationalnews.com reports Iraq arranging a tanker to move oil through the strait.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains at the center of a deepening operational and diplomatic impasse. The most significant development of the past nine hours, per CNBC though not independently confirmed in this feed, is that all U.S. bombers have left a UK air base amid suspected terror plot concerns, alongside reports of further tanker strikes near Iran. The closure and transit picture is contested: Ghalibaf's position that the strait stays closed until Iran's seven conditions are met circulates across multiple outlets including TheCable, Peoples Gazette Nigeria, and India Today, while thenationalnews.com reports Iraq is arranging a tanker to move oil past the strait. S&P Global reports Iraq is separately seeking to buy crude tankers to handle shipments beyond the strait. IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent crude stood at $101.84, down 0.40% over 24 hours, as of 05:52 UTC. Iran's IRGC chief adviser, per Mehr News Agency, claims no U.S. vessel is present in the Persian Gulf, the Strait of Hormuz, the Sea of Oman, or the northern Indian Ocean; that claim originates with Tehran state media. Seventy-six events were indexed in the past 24 hours. As of 05:50 UTC, 215 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, flat over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
